title: Before I fly
intro: Things that work without a Korean number. Do them at home, on good Wi-Fi.

items.text: Install Naver Map and KakaoMap, and switch Naver Map to English.
Install Papago and download the Korean and English offline pack.
Sign up for KakaoTalk with your current number, so it is ready when you land.
Install the Emergency Ready App, set it to English and allow notifications.
Install K.Ride and add your card, so you can call a taxi on day one.
Install Baemin and Shuttle and try to sign up with your current number.
Save key addresses in Korean in your notes: UNIST (울산광역시 울주군 언양읍 유니스트길 50), your dorm, and KTX Ulsan Station (울산역).
Choose a SIM or eSIM. A prepaid plan with a Korean 010 number works on your passport; check whether it supports identity verification (본인인증) and whether you can keep the number after your ARC.
Plan the trip from the airport to Ulsan and book the train or bus.
Bring two cards (Visa or Mastercard) and some cash in won for the first days.
Optional: sign up for Toss with your passport.
Optional: install VISITKOREA and a subway app for weekend trips to Busan or Seoul.

title: First week
intro: Settle in: a working phone, a transit card, campus registration and your way around.

items.text: Get your SIM or activate your eSIM, and note your new 010 number.
Buy a T-money card at a convenience store and top it up with cash. Ulsan city buses are going cashless.
Check in at the dorm. Learn the delivery pickup spot and the waste-sorting rules.
Go to orientation and get your student card and UNIST Portal login. Install UNIST mPortal.
Ask UNIST International Affairs how to apply for your Residence Card (ARC). You must register within 90 days of arrival, in person, with an appointment.
Walk your routes: dorm, classes, cafeteria, the nearest convenience store, pharmacy and bus stop.
Add your Korean number to KakaoTalk and join your class and dorm group chats.
Ask your buddy how exchange students verify on Everytime.
Save the emergency numbers: 112 police, 119 fire and ambulance, 1330 travel helpline, 1345 immigration.
Order delivery once, so you know how it works before you are tired or ill.

title: After I get my ARC
intro: Your Residence Card unlocks the bank account and identity checks most Korean apps ask for.

items.text: Open a bank account and install its app (for example Hana Bank with Hana EZ, or KakaoBank).
Make sure your phone line is registered with your ARC, so identity verification (본인인증) works.
Add your ARC and Korean number to Toss to unlock transfers.
Set up Kakao Pay with your Korean card.
Sign up for Coupang and verify your identity.
Sign up for Karrot for second-hand things.
Try Coupang Eats and Yogiyo now that you have a Korean number.
Optional: try a mobile transit card in T-money GO with your Korean card.
Switch to Kakao T for taxis if K.Ride feels limited.
